items.stem: Clinicians strongly resist a new records system. What is the most effective first leadership response?

options.text: Surface and understand the specific roots of their resistance before responding
options.rationale: Correct: understanding the roots lets leaders address real concerns and separate valid objections.

options.text: Mandate compliance and discipline non-adopters immediately
Ignore the resisters and focus on willing adopters
options.rationale: Ignoring influential sceptics risks the whole change.

options.text: Cancel the change at the first sign of resistance
options.rationale: Abandoning at first resistance wastes the effort.

items.explanation: Correct: understanding the roots lets leaders address real concerns and separate valid objections.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices most help a change actually stick after launch? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Aligning incentives and performance measures with the new behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: incentives that reward the new behaviour reinforce it.
Correct: visible early wins build momentum and belief.

options.text: Removing the sponsor once launch is done
options.rationale: Withdrawing sponsorship too early lets change fade.
Unchanged old incentives pull people back.

items.explanation: Correct: incentives that reward the new behaviour reinforce it.

items.stem: A change programme created intense urgency but people are now exhausted and disengaged. What does this most likely indicate?

options.text: Urgency was generated without pacing and reinforcement, exceeding change capacity
options.rationale: Correct: urgency without regard for capacity and pacing produces fatigue and disengagement.
Fatigue points to overload, not modest ambition.
Exhaustion is not the same as acceptance.
This does not follow from fatigue.

items.explanation: Correct: urgency without regard for capacity and pacing produces fatigue and disengagement.
